subject: social-studies
title: Water Supply: From Rain to Tap, Stage by Stage

segments.say: Stage 1: rain is collected in a reservoir. Rain falls on the catchment and the reservoir stores it as raw water - it looks clear, but it still carries dirt and germs and the cleanliness bar is low. Point at the cleanliness bar on your student notes before treatment starts to lift it.
questions: Where is the rain collected, and what is the collected water called?
Why is this water not yet safe to drink, even though it looks clear?

segments.say: Stage 2: raw water is drawn to the treatment works. Pipes carry the raw water out of the reservoir to the treatment works, and the bar barely moves - moving water does not clean it. Now try the journey question on your worksheet.
questions: Where does the raw water go after the reservoir, and how does it get there?
Why does the cleanliness bar barely move during this stage?

segments.say: Stage 3: treatment cleans the water, stage by stage. Dirt settles and sinks in the first tank, germs are trapped and removed in the next, and the cleanliness bar climbs 70 to 140 to 210 to 280 as each stage removes more. Check the stage order against your student notes before moving on.
questions: What does each treatment stage remove from the water?
How far does the cleanliness bar climb at each treatment stage?

segments.say: Stage 4: clean water is stored and piped to home taps. Only now - treated first - is the water stored and piped home, and the bar is full. The shortcut of drinking straight from the reservoir skips every cleaning stage. Keep the whole order - reservoir, treatment works, cleaned and stored, home taps - in view as you check your student notes and finish the exit ticket.
questions: What must happen to the water before it is stored and piped home?
What is the whole journey, in order, with no stage skipped?
segments.watchFor: Tap water is clean as soon as it is collected, because rainwater and reservoir water are already safe to drink. Listen for students who treat clear-looking collected water as ready to drink. Send them back to the treatment stages: Collected water is raw water, not tap water: it is drawn from the reservoir to the treatment works, where treatment stages remove dirt and germs step by step, and only the cleaned water is stored and piped to home taps.
